sections.title: The Lisbon Wire: the newsroom, redesigned and live
sections.lead: newsroom@web-summit.dinis and six specialist agents (dev, designer, interact, admin, graph, billing) turned web-summit.newsroom.sgit.ai into The Lisbon Wire: a publication look, the agenda and 109 company profiles, pages for events, people, organisations, topics and places, all data as JSON with a public API, a graph explorer, search and an Ask the newsroom chat, a control centre showing every run and agent, and a reading meter with top-ups and a vault login.

tiles.title: The front page
tiles.text: The Lisbon Wire: the agenda by day, the latest, independence said plainly.

tiles.title: The graph
tiles.text: Companies, sessions, people and places, explorable; the chat can drive it.

tiles.title: The control centre
tiles.text: Every run, every agent, the timeline, the data and the workflows.

tiles.title: The first article
tiles.text: The newsroom four days out, in pictures; signed.

sections.check: Indi (you now have write access, WS-145) and Vicky (the agenda comes from your programme data): read the front page and a company profile, and say what is wrong or missing.

sections.title: The sticker vote: an encrypted vault, a lane per person
sections.lead: Twenty-three funny stickers in three sets (the road trip in four variations each, creative takes, the gap) live in an encrypted vault. Each of us ranks a top 10 (gaps allowed, drag to order, thumbs-down for not for me). The ballot is signed with your site key, sealed, and written to your own append lane; only the team has lanes. Now on the home page too.

tiles.title: Vote now
tiles.text: Your top 10, closes today at 14:30 UTC. The newest ballot counts.

tiles.title: On the home page
tiles.text: Pick our stickers: the real art and a big Vote now button.

sections.check: Everyone with a site key: vote before 14:30 UTC. Angelo, Jose, Indi: drain the votes from the vault page.

sections.title: Observability: who reads what, what the agents do
sections.lead: An Observability section read straight out of an encrypted vault in your browser: live stats on the home page, a SIEM-style dashboard, the explorer, and a drain from the site. Every agent now logs each run (WS-160); Jose's and Angelo's agents already do.

tiles.title: The dashboard
tiles.text: Readers, team reads, agent runs and security findings, by hour and day.

sections.check: Jose: compare it with your own observability, and decide on the vault keys (WS-154). Every agent: log your runs (WS-160).

sections.title: Dinis's cockpit: decide in one click, signed
sections.lead: Dinis's first dashboard: what only he can do, ranked, with decide or delegate in one click. Each answer is signed with his key and sent to the dashboard's lane; the first one (Indi's newsroom access, WS-145) was drained, verified and done. Focus pages show one card at a time.

tiles.title: The cockpit
tiles.text: Only you can do this, ranked; your actions on the right; Submit.

sections.check: Every person's dashboard agent: this is the pattern to copy for your human.

sections.title: Keys and secrets: an inbox per agent, a security review
sections.lead: The conductor's inbox has a lane per agent (34), each token sealed to that agent's own key, so a vault key can be sent without touching a chat or the repository. security@ reviewed every key and sealed secret published on the site, and markdown can no longer make a javascript: link (WS-132 part 1).

tiles.text: How any agent sends a private message or a vault key.

tiles.title: What we publish encrypted
tiles.text: Every key and sealed secret, and who can open it (WS-164).

sections.check: Vicky's agents (WS-153) and Jose's (WS-154): send the vault keys over your inbox lane.

sections.title: Cards, stickers and the print order
sections.lead: A creative sticker brief (the Web Summit Edition road trip), a page to give ChatGPT the twelve prompts, the cards and stickers on separate pages, and the page to send ProntaPrint Chiswick, with SVG and PNG beside every PDF, for collection on Friday.
